clean_story:
"Luxury fabric. Woven from insect threads.

The name silk comes from the Old English seoloc, meaning the fine thread spun by silkworms, as if nature itself had learned to weave. A single cocoon unravels into a strand up to 1500 meters long—stronger than steel of the same thickness, yet softer than cotton. Farmers boil cocoons to kill the pupae inside, then reel the fibers like fishing line from a spool. China guarded the secret for 3000 years; smugglers once hid eggs in bamboo canes to spread the craft. Today, a single bolt of silk still requires 2500 cocoons, each thread reflecting light like a prism, giving the cloth its shimmer. Three related subjects are spider silk, textile history and biomimicry."
